rows.why: S1 is about cleaning case and surrounding whitespace before matching, which is item 2's question. Its pick trims and lowercases, and the run shows "  DRAFT " reading as 'draft', so " PUBLISHED ", "Merged" and "claimed" become their lowercase statuses.

Item 3 asks which old spellings map to a status. Its pick maps only 'in review'; the run shows 'done' and 'in progress' reading as null. So "under_review" and "LIVE" would read as null, not 'review' and 'published'.

Item 1 asks what an unknown stored value reads as. Its pick returns null instead of guessing the nearest status (readStatus("banana") → null), and item 7 shows empty and whitespace-only values also read as null. That matches 'no status at all, never the nearest one'.
No item asks what writing a valid status does. Item 4 is about rejecting variants; its run happens to show writeStatus("draft") → 'draft', but that is not the question it asks.

Item 4 asks whether writing accepts variants and old spellings. Its pick accepts only exact lowercase enum strings; the run shows "Draft", " draft" and "in-review" all throw. Item 5 shows the error message quotes the value as given ("Bogus").

Item 9 asks how readStatuses reports unreadable values. Its pick and run list the raw stored strings, de-duplicated and sorted, which matches 'each distinct original value once, sorted, exactly as stored'. Item 8 confirms each unreadable row comes back with status null.
